claims.text: The target material may be a metallic or ceramic engineering material with multiphase structures and/or a coarse microstructure.
A data-driven machine-learning framework can integrate high-throughput experimental and simulation datasets.
The framework can predictively adjust thermal-cycle profiles, strain rates, and cooling rates.
The machine-learning framework can simultaneously enhance phase stability, refine microstructure, and optimize material properties.
A model can map processing conditions to phase-equilibrium, microstructural, and property outcomes.
The model can be used in a closed loop to adapt processing parameters in real time.
High-throughput experimental and computational datasets can support controlled variation of temperature, strain, and cooling rate during thermomechanical processing.
Refined grains and controlled phase distributions mediate enhanced stability and property optimization.
An integrated machine-learning framework can quantify interdependencies among thermal cycles, mechanical deformation, and microstructural evolution.
Iterative model-based adjustment of processing parameters enables simultaneous control of phase stability and microstructure.
Simultaneous control of phase stability and microstructure leads to improved overall properties.
ML-guided processing will reduce undesirable phase transformations relative to conventional fixed-parameter processing.
ML-guided processing will produce smaller and more uniform grains or precipitates.
ML-guided processing will enhance mechanical or functional properties relative to traditional fixed-parameter methods.
Traditional stepwise thermomechanical treatments are commonly optimized separately through trial and error.
Traditional processing often entails a strength-ductility trade-off or incomplete control of phase stability.
The approach is expected to work when processing parameters can be reliably varied and measured.
Applicability outside the training-data range or to systems with substantially different thermomechanical behavior is uncertain.
Early evidence supports the potential of data-driven optimization to address complex property interdependencies.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements over conventionally processed controls would falsify the proposed unified-optimization hypothesis.
